Marketing and Advertising Policy > Overview > Purpose of this policy > This policy aims to

- Ensure all marketing and advertising is truthful, transparent, and fully compliant with relevant CBUAE and UAE regulations.
- Establish an approval process, including mandatory prior CBUAE approval for communications involving industry-wide impacts or references to the regulator.
- Prevent misleading claims, exaggeration, or discriminatory content that could harm Nebras’s reputation or the ecosystem’s integrity.
- Support Nebras’s role in fostering trust by clearly communicating its neutral position as infrastructure operator, scheme brand, and standard setter — without endorsing specific financial products, TPPs, or LFIs.

Marketing and Advertising Policy > Scope & definitions > What this policy covers

- The AlTareq brand and trust-mark.
- Advertisements, brochures, and promotional materials.
- Social media posts, website content, and email marketing campaigns.
- Industry publicity, marketing events, and national awareness campaigns.

The policy does not apply to confidential engagements conducted bilaterally or multilaterally with the industry (including product development and other consultations), nor to product or standards collateral circulated in the ecosystem. Industry conferences and similar non-marketing activities are conducted at the discretion of the CEO.

Marketing and Advertising Policy > Scope & definitions > What this policy covers > Definitions

- Industry-wide activity — any marketing or communication that affects or targets multiple LFIs, TPPs, or the entire Open Finance ecosystem, such as ecosystem adoption drives.
- CBUAE-related messaging — content that references the CBUAE, its logos, or regulatory approvals, or implies endorsement by the regulator.
- (National) campaigns — broad, public-facing initiatives to promote Open Finance across the UAE, often involving media partnerships or public events.

chunks.text:
Marketing and Advertising Policy > Core principles > Principles guiding Nebras marketing

- Truthfulness — all statements must be accurate, evidence-based, and verifiable, avoiding unsubstantiated claims about benefits or performance.
- Transparency — clearly disclose Nebras’s role, any limitations of services, and disclaimers regarding liability or endorsements.
- Fairness — ensure content is inclusive, non-discriminatory, and does not favour specific participants.
- Compliance — strictly adhere to CBUAE Circulars and UAE media standards, including prohibitions on false advertising.

chunks.text:
Marketing and Advertising Policy > Approval process > How marketing materials are approved

The Nebras team drafts materials and submits them to the CEO for initial review, ensuring alignment with policy principles. For national campaigns, additional sign-off from the Chairman is required to confirm strategic fit.

Review timeline: 7–14 business days, with revisions tracked.

Industry-wide activities or CBUAE-related messaging must be submitted to the CBUAE Communications team at least 14 days in advance. Approval must be obtained in writing, with any required modifications implemented before release.

All materials are routed through the CPO for logging. No unauthorised releases are permitted; digital tools may be used for efficiency.

chunks.text:
Marketing and Advertising Policy > Controls & restrictions > What is controlled and restricted

- Content restrictions — prohibit exaggeration of ecosystem benefits; include mandatory disclaimers for any regulatory references or potential risks.
- Social media controls — all posts must be pre-approved by the CEO or CPO; staff personal accounts may not promote Nebras without authorisation.
- Third-party endorsements — any collaboration requires written agreements, CEO/CPO review, and compliance checks to ensure alignment with Nebras’s neutrality.
- Recordkeeping — maintain detailed logs of all approvals, revisions, and releases for a minimum of 5 years in a secure database.

Marketing and Advertising Policy > Responsibilities > Who does what

- Chief Product Officer (CPO) — oversees content creation, internal approvals, and coordination with external parties.
- CBUAE Communications team — reviews and provides input on all industry-wide materials, or those involving CBUAE-related content or branding.
- CEO — grants final internal sign-off and ensures regulatory compliance.
- Staff and contractors — submit all proposed materials to the CPO, adhere to restrictions, and report any potential violations immediately.

Marketing and Advertising Policy > Training & oversight > Training, monitoring, and enforcement > Training and awareness

- Annual mandatory training for all staff on this policy, including CBUAE Circulars, Federal Laws, and UAE media standards.
- Topics include identifying compliant content, navigating approval processes, social media best practices, and recognising misleading claims.

Marketing and Advertising Policy > Training & oversight > Training, monitoring, and enforcement > Monitoring and reporting

- Monitoring — the CPO conducts annual reviews of ongoing campaigns to verify compliance and effectiveness.
- Reporting — an annual report to the Board detailing activities, approval metrics, any breaches, and lessons learned.
- Escalation — detected non-compliance is reported to the CEO immediately, with severe issues escalated to the CBUAE where they involve regulatory violations.

- Violations, such as releasing unapproved materials or making misleading claims, are likely to result in disciplinary measures.
- Systemic or repeated issues are reported to the CBUAE for potential regulatory enforcement.
